arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: the sides that brought the case argue the statute lacks explicit rights-creating language. They cite Gonzaga for the requirement of clear language. They argue private rights are exceptions in the Spending Clause context.

the opposing sides argue the statute imposes clear obligations on states. They assert the state knows its obligations run to individuals. They argue the text, context, and structure confirm a private right exists.

Justice Kagan noted the state knows its obligation runs to individuals. Justice Sotomayor questioned the distinction between benefits and rights. Justice Thomas asked how to amend the statute for clarity.
